feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. The evidence is iteration 1 (±0.03 m span, y=0.05 m, 12 mm; score 69.32, reproduced exactly in iteration 4), which is the reference for this single-variable change. Line loss has stayed at about 1 per run across iterations 0 to 4 (1.0 to 1.65 per run), and it did not fall when the footprint went to 16 mm (iteration 2, score 54.45). The span change from ±0.024 to ±0.03 m raised the score by about 15 points in iteration 1, though that change was paired with a controller change, so the span effect is only partly isolated. Iteration 3 showed that y=0.03 m lost about 10 points with the same controller, so keep y=0.05 m. Steering oscillation has stayed between 0.09 and 0.15, so it is not the limiting factor. Please note that at ±0.04 m with 20 mm spacing and 12 mm footprints there is an 8 mm gap between the centre and the ±0.02 m sensors. This should not cause line loss, since the 25 mm tape always covers at least one footprint, but it may make readings dip as the line crosses that gap. Do not treat any of this as a result for the current candidate. Next race: if line_loss_events falls clearly below about 1 per run and progress rises, a wider 5-sensor span of ±0.05 m is worth considering as a later separate test. If line loss stays at about 1 per run, return to the ±0.03 m span and hold the geometry; do not move the forward offset again without a controller explanation.
